legend.notes: Sentences quoted verbatim from the catalog page that state a condition we could NOT express as structure — exclusions ("Research courses may not be used"), eligibility lists, per-course grade minimums. A section can consist of nothing but these. Quote them; never infer from them that a particular course does or does not satisfy the section.
legend.creditsRequired: Semester hours the catalog states for a section whose courses it does not list. Do not add these into a program total: some restate credit that another section already counts.

notes: Registration in the following course is required if the thesis is not completed by the conclusion of the term of registration for MSCI 7990:

requirementSections.title: Concentrations
notes: Completing a concentration is required to complete this program. A minimum of 12 semester hours is required.

footnotes.text: Students who have not completed their thesis but have already registered for the required number of thesis hours, and have no remaining coursework to complete the degree, may register for Thesis Continuation—Half-Time (MSCI 7996) in their last semester (including summer term). There is a 1-semester-hour tuition charge for Thesis Continuation—Half-Time (MSCI 7996). Thesis Continuation may be taken only once.
Additional expenses may be associated with the experience courses, which are offered on-ground in a weeklong experiential format.
Some of the optional experiential learning experiences are limited to specific groups of medical or allied health professionals.

One semester hour of Experiential Reflections: Bridging Theory and Experience (MSCI 5400) must be completed for each experience course. Experiential Reflections: Bridging Theory and Experience (MSCI 5400) may be taken concurrently or after the associated courses.

Students who select AI Across the Health Sciences (HLTH 5800) (4 semester hours) vs. Workforce Metrics: Measuring, Comparing, and Privileging the Interprofessional Healthcare Team (MSCI 6002) (3 semester hours) will incur an additional 1-semester-hour cost beyond the total program credits.
Anatomy and Physiology I and II, or equivalent, and an exercise physiology or medical background are strongly recommended for the exercise science concentration.
Physical Activity and Exercise: Prescription, Measurement, and Testing (EXSC 5210) is offered online with a four-day, on-campus, hands-on lab component in a low-residency format.
